line: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 f4 dxe5 fxe5 Nc6 Be3 Bf5 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Be7 Be2 f6 O-O O-O exf6 Bxf6
teaches: After a central break is resolved, recapture with the piece that ends up doing the most, not the one nearest to hand. A bishop that lands on the long diagonal turns the opened centre into pressure on the pawn that is left — the break was never about the pawn count.
explains: The bishop takes on f6, where it bears down the diagonal on the pawn on d4 and connects with the queen behind it. The chain that was cramping the position is gone and its remaining pawn is now the target.
